judged_text: The addMembers action neither returns the model.addMembers promise nor has any in-flight guard or input clearing, so concurrent invocations interleave and the committed input state desyncs from the server. Double-clicking the Add button issues overlapping PUT requests; and because the username input is never cleared after a successful add (the TODO), the same usernames remain in the selector and are re-submitted on the next click, while the controller gives the caller no promise to observe success/failure — a failed add leaves the input populated as if it had been consumed.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` but does not `return` that promise and has no in-flight/disable guard; it also explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and indeed never clears `usernames` after success. This is a concrete UX/robustness issue grounded in the diff, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it causes incorrect membership state (duplicate adds may be idempotent server-side and concurrent reloads end up consistent).
